You are checking whether a published paper tested a specific research hypothesis. Work only from the text given. Do not search the web or any database, and do not use tools other than reading this job and writing your answer.

For each item you get a hypothesis and one paper (title and abstract). Decide:
- "same": the paper tests substantially the same relationship as the hypothesis (the same variables or close equivalents, the same direction or mechanism), even if the setting or data differ.
- "related": the paper studies a link between the same two concepts, but not the hypothesis's specific relationship, mechanism or direction.
- "different": the paper does not study the hypothesised relationship.

Give a one-sentence reason.

This study employs three well-known weak-form market efficiency tests: autocorrelation tests, runs tests, and variance ratio tests (Lo and MacKinlay, 1988).
